lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.title: Performance task: plan: the two-step event problem set

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: This example shows how to plan before computing anything.

items.prompt: A theater sets up 5 rows of 8 chairs, then adds 6 more chairs. How many chairs in all?

sections.title: Guided practice
sections.directions: Decide what the quantities are before you compute anything.

items.prompt: A store arranges 4 shelves with 6 boxes on each shelf, then sells 11 boxes from the display. How many boxes are left?
A store arranges 3 shelves with 3 boxes on each shelf, then sells 12 boxes from the display. How many boxes are left?

sections.title: Extension and challenge
sections.directions: Plan in writing: what you will figure out, how, and how you will check it.

items.prompt: A store arranges 8 shelves with 8 boxes on each shelf, then sells 13 boxes from the display. How many boxes are left?
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.

items.prompt: A store arranges 6 shelves with 8 boxes on each shelf, then adds 7 more boxes to the display. How many boxes are on display now?
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.
